ports.note: Takes a table and gives back the same table with fewer rows. Key columns, value field and unit are unchanged, because selecting rows does not change what the table measures.

ontology.note: No ontology mapping yet. The receipt names the column, the values kept, how many rows were kept and dropped, and any named value the table did not hold.

changes.description: Show me how it works, in Configure…: a made-up table checked row by row under the way of choosing you have picked: values to keep, values to leave out, or a range; a row with an empty cell is set aside by keeping values and kept by leaving one out, as this step does; its last step the table this step makes from the same rows (experiment 223).

evidence.note: Unit tested on the same Table IX fixture, including the ordering the named values impose and a value absent from the table. Nothing here establishes that a selection is an honest one: keeping a subset of categories is exactly how a figure can mislead, and the widget cannot tell a partition from a cherry-pick. The range is unit tested (tests/select-a-range.test.mjs) and built from an empty canvas through the dialog in tests/select-range.browser.mjs, Chromium. 0.5.0: tests/table-walkthroughs.test.mjs holds the walkthrough to this step's own function under every choice it follows; tests/table-walkthroughs.browser.mjs opens it from Configure…, Chromium and WebKit.
